newsitem.title: DUBAI: Filipino stabbed to death in Saudi Arabia.
newsitem.headline: Filipino stabbed to death in Saudi Arabia.

text.p: A Filipino clothes shop owner in Saudi Arabia was stabbed to death in his home in the eastern Saudi city of al-Khobar, a Philippine embassy official said on Wednesday.
The body of Amoran Macausor, a Filipino Moslem who had lived in the kingdom for about 14 years, was found by police in his apartment on Saturday, the official in the capital Riyadh said.
"He was killed brutally, stabbed several times in his abdomen, neck and parts of his back," the official told Reuters. "The police are still investigating and we don't know who could be suspected."

Macausor, who was in his early 40s and a leading member of the Filipino community in al-Khobar, owned a men's garment store together with a Saudi partner. The official said Macausor was well-known in al-Khobar as well as Riyadh.
"The family is due to come to Saudi Arabia once they get their travel papers," the official said. The victim's wife is a student in the Philippines.
Macausor was originally from the town of Maguing on the Philippines' island of Mindanao.
About half a million Filipinos live and work in Saudi Arabia. Some four million Filipinos work overseas -- about a million of them in the Gulf -- in hopes of earning more than they can at home.
